subject: Technical evaluation milestone — draft timeline & targets
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Technical evaluation milestone — draft timeline & targets

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed draft for the MAP milestone focused on the technical evaluation so we can align on owners, success criteria, and dates. I tried to keep the ask minimal so procurement/ML can slot this into their queue.

Proposed MAP milestone: Technical evaluation plan (what we need Redwood + HealthGrid to do)
- Objective: Validate candidate models for HealthGrid conversational triage and note extraction on the 100K prompt sample.
- Success criteria (pass = all must be met):
  - Accuracy: Intent F1 >= 0.85 and entity extraction F1 >= 0.80 on the sample prompt set
  - Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end < 300ms for 256-token responses under target concurrency (p50/p95 to be reported)
  - Cost: baseline inference unit cost <= $0.60 per 1k tokens (measured on Redwood Hosted baseline)
  - Long-context check: 99th percentile for 1k-token flows documented (see dependencies)
- Model shortlist (suggested): Redwood-Open-7B-q4, Llama-3-13B-ptq, Falcon-40B-instruct (evaluation on quantized variants and a float baseline)

Proposed owners / responsibilities
- HealthGrid: provide labeled sample set, designate ML lead to run private env runs and confirm acceptance tests (owner: HealthGrid ML)
- Redwood: provide benchmark harness, baseline hosted results, measurement script, and initial model config suggestions (owner: Redwood infra + eval team)
- Joint: agree on final prompt set, metrics script, and gating thresholds prior to runs

Timeline (draft)
- Apr 22: Kick-off + share prompts and benchmark spec
- Apr 29 — May 6: HealthGrid private runs + Redwood hosted baseline runs
- May 10: Evaluation readout and go/no-go decision for next milestone
- Target close: May 31 (moving to contracting/PO on success)

Dependencies / blockers
- Tokenization alignment and sample prompt export from your environment
- Procurement sandbox access if HealthGrid wants to run in dedicated capacity
- NDA/SOW addendum for logs/PII handling (if required)

Next steps
- Can you confirm the ML lead and procurement contact so we can add them to the MAP and share the benchmark spec?
- Lauren will attach the benchmark spec template and harness link in the next note.

Attachments referenced: benchmark_spec.xlsx (template), example_prompts.jsonl (sample prompts) — I will attach these in follow-up.

Thanks —
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap and the proposed milestone. This looks sensible. A few notes from our side:

1) ML ownership: Jamal Harris (copied) will lead the runs on our side and owns the labeled set. He'll confirm sample export by EOD Tue (Apr 20).
2) Prompt set size: we plan to share ~80k prompts, with a focused 10k validation slice that is labeled for metrics.
3) Additional long-context requirement: please include a long-context pass for 1k-token prompts — we care about worst-case tails. For that pass, can you propose a 99th percentile latency target?
4) Procurement: procurement@healthgrid.com is on copy; they will likely request an SOW and DPA addendum before we allow Redwood-hosted runs on any production data. Can you indicate minimal SOW language or a template?

I attached an initial prompt sample and a short goals doc for the benchmarks (initial_benchmark_goals.docx, example_prompts.jsonl).

If we can get the benchmark spec and harness link today/tomorrow we can schedule the kick-off for Apr 22 as proposed. Jamal — can you confirm your availability for Apr 22?

Emma

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical evaluation milestone — draft timeline & targets

Emma / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the example prompts. A few technical clarifications from the Redwood infra/evals side so the runs are apples-to-apples:

- Measurement harness: we will provide a reproducible script and docker image (link below) that reports p50/p95/p99 latency, token-level throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. Please use the harness for the joint readout.
- Warm-up & KV cache: for models with KV caching the first few requests skew latency — we recommend a 10-request warm-up and report both warmed and cold tails.
- Batch sizing & concurrency: please run with two profiles: (A) single-user latency (concurrency=1, batch=1) and (B) throughput profile (concurrency=16, batch=8) so we can show realistic production tradeoffs.
- Long-context (1k tokens): for the 1k-token pass propose we use p99 latency target <= 1200ms on dedicated hardware; we will capture large-context degradation curves.
- Quantization matrix: suggested starting configs in the spreadsheet I attached (q4_0/q8_0 mixed-run suggestions).

Ownership commitments
- Redwood Eval Team: supply harness, run hosted baseline (Redwood Hosted) for all shortlisted models, publish JSON results to shared drive by May 6.
- HealthGrid ML (Jamal): run private environment experiments using the same harness and share raw results by May 6.

I attached the benchmark_spec.xlsx (template) and left a short notes tab with the run commands we will execute. Also dropping the proposed harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-harness/tree/proposals/healthgrid

If this looks good we'll lock the kick-off for Apr 22 10:00am PT and sync on procurement items in parallel.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Developer Relations | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com
